units.translation: perfect of the verb εἴκω [to be like], whose second and third persons are ἔοικας [you are like], ἔοικε [he/she/it is like], participle εἰκώς [being like]: for only these forms are found in Aeschylus, meaning 'like' or 'equal'.
I seem, I seem to myself.
The participle εἰκός [being like], which is used adjectivally, see in its own place.
With more she bears, but like her own offspring.
For like a stranger, with a complete net, I will come.
And the Cyprian stamp, like in womanly forms, has been struck.
You seem to revel in the present circumstances.
You seem to say nothing of what your father desires.
Speaking, I seem to say many things in vain.
But having come, he seems not to make a trade of battle.
Now a source of evils seems to have been found for all friends.
The stranger seems to need a clear interpreter.
She seems to be about to prophesy concerning her own evils.
The stranger seems to be like a keen-scented dog.
I seem to be about to prophesy soon.
But he seems, bright at the rising of the sun, to be about to come breathing.
The stranger seems to be plotting evil.
Now her neck seems to be about to fall near the razor's edge.
You seem to be about to kill—your mother.
I seem to lament in vain, living, at the tomb.
You seem to be about to enchant me.
I seem to be about to drag you.
He seems to be about to proclaim.

festival. Ironically Apollo, after he had reviewed the Furies' functions.

unless Plato, when he rendered Aeschylus's words in indirect speech, substituted ἑάς [his own] for ἐμάς [my own].

proclaiming to the gods prayers that bring fulfillment.

I bring upon.
Thus I corrected what is in M: ποῖ δ᾽ ἔτι τέλος ἐπάγει θεός [where then does the god bring an end?].
But where, having advanced, will the god bring an end?
He brings Ares, tamer of the bow, upon spear-famed men.
But upon me he brought a relish for his bed, for my luxury.
bringing another ruin upon ruin.
where then does the god bring an end?

a shout that brings on madness.

I sing over.
Who could call back the black blood by singing over it?
to revere
I revere.
But you did not revere the holy majesty of my thighs.
to praise, approve
I praise, approve.
Equivalent to παραινώ [I advise], I advise.
These things I praise in you.
The city at different times praises different just things.
I am filled from all sides to praise her.
You will praise this speech.
I advise you to send wise and noble men as rowers against him.
But I advise you not to disgrace me.
And I advise you to keep a reverent tongue.
I advise

who is at fault.

Unless I do something to the guilty ones.

heeding nothing of the gods.
